Hi Ravi —

Thanks for the clear examples and for attaching the invoice. I've pulled this into our billing and product teams for a short write-up; below is a concise, authoritative explanation we use on Redwood hosted billing. I include a worked example using your numbers.

Summary (short answers)
- System messages: counted as input tokens. Any text included in the API request as a system message is billed as part of the request input.
- Tool calls: billing depends on how the tool output flows back into model interactions.
  - If the model invokes a tool and the tool returns text that is NOT passed back into the model (client-side consumption only), that tool output is NOT billed as model output tokens.
  - If the tool output is returned to the model as part of the next model request (e.g., you perform a tool call, then send tool results back as model input for a follow-up generation), those tool-returned tokens are billed as input tokens on that subsequent request.
- Rounding/granularity: Redwood charges on a per-token basis (whole tokens). For streaming requests we estimate interim usage but finalize counts on request completion and always bill whole tokens. There is no fractional-token billing on the final invoice; we sum whole-token counts across all requests in the billing period.

Worked example with your numbers (how we would count them)
- Initial request payload (single request): system message = 6 tokens (input), user prompt = 48 tokens (input) => input so far = 54 tokens.
- Model generates 412 tokens during the response phase => model output = 412 tokens.
- Model triggers a tool call; tool returns 320 tokens. Two paths: 
  A) If the tool return was consumed client-side and never fed back to the model, Redwood does NOT count the 320 tool tokens as model input or output. Billing for that session: input 54 + output 412 => 466 billed tokens.
  B) If the tool return was passed back into the model in a follow-up request (for example you send the 320 tokens into the model as part of a new user/system message), then those 320 tokens are counted as input tokens on that follow-up request and billed in that follow-up's token totals. If that follow-up produced X output tokens, those would be billed as X output tokens.

On your invoice line that shows 786 output tokens: that looks like an aggregation/attribution issue where the tool-returned text was likely included in the billed output bucket. I will escalate to billing to reconcile the specific invoice lines and make an adjustment if our system misattributed tool text as model output.

Notes / caveats
- Streaming: partial tokens emitted in stream chunks are buffered; final counts are rounded to whole tokens per completed request. If a request is aborted mid-generation, we finalize counts at the abort point (again, whole tokens).
- Tool integrations: some partner tool integrations are proxied in ways where the returned text is captured in server logs and can be included in downstream prompts; the billing behavior follows the path the data takes (billed only when it's part of a model input or produced by the model).

Next steps

- For the commercial part: Ben (copied) will follow up on a short-term credit or commitment-based discount while we reconcile the invoice.
